findings.explanation: google_storage_bucket.logs_access (line 30) is created with the explicit comment "Dedicated bucket to receive access logs for the main logs bucket", and both google_storage_bucket.logs and .logs_access carry a `# holden:ignore:HLD_GCP_003` suppression whose own checkov rationale says self-logging would create a cycle — implying the intended fix is for `logs` to log to `logs_access` instead of to itself. But `logs` never gets a `logging` block pointing at `logs_access`, so the dedicated bucket sits empty and access logging on the log-destination bucket (which itself receives the state bucket's access logs) is silently disabled entirely. The deterministic HLD_GCP_003 check cannot catch this: it's explicitly suppressed on this resource, and even unsuppressed it has no way to know a *specific* companion bucket (logs_access, not just any bucket) was the intended target.
findings.remediation: Add to google_storage_bucket.logs: a logging block pointing at logs_access.
findings.suppression_reason: User decision (2026-08-02): a log-destination bucket doesn't need its own access logging; logs_access is not required to be wired up to logs. Accepted as-is, not a gap.
findings.title: logs_access bucket is provisioned but never receives the logs it was created for

findings.explanation: HLD_CI_017 already flags both workflow calls as unpinned (uses ...@main). What the deterministic check can't see, because it doesn't cross-reference CI config with the Terraform IAM role defined in the same repo, is the actual blast radius: verify.yml runs on every push to main with permissions contents:write and id-token:write, and calls JamesWoolfenden/.github/.github/workflows/terraform-verify-gcp.yml@main — a mutable ref in a different repo. Anyone who can push to that ref's main branch can inject steps that (a) push to this repo's main branch and (b) mint a federated GCP token for terraform-gcp-statebucket@pike-477416.iam.gserviceaccount.com. .pike/pike.generated_policy.tf documents that this exact service account is intended to hold storage.buckets.create/delete/get/setIamPolicy/update project-wide (not scoped to just the state bucket). Confidence is medium rather than high because the actual IAM binding granting that role to the CI SA lives outside this repo and isn't visible here — the pike file documents the intended/expected grant, not a verified one.
findings.remediation: Pin both workflow calls (verify.yml:18, pull_request.yml:16) to a full commit SHA of JamesWoolfenden/.github, annotated with the resolved branch as a comment, as HLD_CI_017 already recommends. Given the credential this unlocks, treat this as higher priority than a typical unpinned-action finding.
findings.suppression_reason: User decision (2026-08-02): accepted risk, org-controlled repo (JamesWoolfenden/.github) — suppressed via # holden:ignore:HLD_CI_017 on both pull_request.yml and verify.yml.
findings.title: Unpinned reusable workflow call carries write access + federated cloud credentials into a role that can delete/re-IAM any bucket in the project

findings.explanation: google_storage_bucket.logs (11-27) and google_storage_bucket.logs_access (30-46) are identical in every attribute (uniform_bucket_level_access, public_access_prevention, versioning, encryption) except the name. This is example code so the cost is low, but a for_each over a small map of {logs, logs_access} would remove the duplication and make it obvious the two buckets are meant to be configured identically.
findings.remediation: Collapse into a single resource with for_each over the two bucket names, or leave as-is if the two-bucket-role split is meant to stay visually distinct for teaching purposes.
findings.title: logs and logs_access are near-duplicate resource blocks
